title: Verifier Verdict Contract
description: Machine-checkable form of a mandatory verifier's output. Severity grammar, the mandatory closing verdict, and the summary line are grounded verbatim in conductor/review-output-standards.md ('Severity-Tiered Output Format', 'Mandatory Closing Verdict', 'Review Summary Line'). The primary-artifacts-only requirement and the six named verifiers are grounded in conductor/verification-routing.md ('Routing Table', 'Verifier Brief Standard'). review-output-standards.md defines THREE distinct per-role closing-verdict vocabularies (Quinn/Reid: BLOCK | APPROVE WITH SUGGESTIONS | APPROVE; Cyra: BLOCK | CONDITIONAL PASS | CLEAR; Leah: HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW confidence, no disposition at all). This schema normalizes all three onto one canonical `disposition` axis (BLOCK | APPROVE_WITH_SUGGESTIONS | APPROVE) so a single ship-gate check works across every verifier, and preserves the agent's literal wording in `role_verdict_raw` for traceability. Mapping: CLEAR -> APPROVE, CONDITIONAL PASS -> APPROVE_WITH_SUGGESTIONS, BLOCK -> BLOCK; Leah's confidence tiers are a separate, non-disposition axis carried in `confidence`. Phase 0 / Design Decision #3.

verifier.description: verification-routing.md Routing Table — the six named mandatory verifiers.

output_domain.description: verification-routing.md Routing Table column 1, e.g. 'Code diff / PR', 'Security', 'Research / intelligence claims'.

primary_artifacts_read.description: verification-routing.md: 'the diff, the logs, the URLs, the file paths — never Tess's summary of those artifacts. A verifier that reads the orchestrator's summary inherits the orchestrator's confabulations and verifies nothing.' Required non-empty so a verdict cannot exist without at least one primary artifact the verifier claims to have read itself.

findings.description: review-output-standards.md 'Severity-Tiered Output Format': every finding is [SEVERITY] area/file:line — finding — risk — fix/action.

severity_counts.description: Must match the actual tally of findings[] by severity — checked as a lint rule by tessctl validate (review-output-standards.md 'Review Summary Line': 'Found [N] CRITICAL, [N] HIGH, [N] MEDIUM, [N] LOW').

summary_line.description: review-output-standards.md 'Review Summary Line', e.g. 'Reviewed [scope]. Found [N] CRITICAL, [N] HIGH, [N] MEDIUM, [N] LOW. Top priority: [description].'

disposition.description: Canonical closing verdict, normalized from review-output-standards.md's per-role grammar (see top-level description).

role_verdict_raw.description: The verifier's literal per-role wording, e.g. 'CLEAR', 'CONDITIONAL PASS', 'Confidence: HIGH' — preserved for traceability back to review-output-standards.md's exact vocabulary.

confidence.description: Leah's confidence axis (research/intelligence verdicts) — a separate axis from disposition, not a substitute for it. review-output-standards.md 'Leah (Research & Intelligence)' section.

then.$comment: review-output-standards.md severity table: CRITICAL 'Must be fixed before merge/deploy. Blocks approval.' A verdict cannot declare a CRITICAL finding and a non-BLOCK disposition — this is the schema check that makes 'tests pass, ship it' impossible to cash when a CRITICAL finding is present.
